title: JsonUI Test Results
description: Standardized test-run results emitted by all platform drivers; consumed by `jsonui-test report`

failureReason.description: Machine-readable counterpart to 'error', which is prose and changes between releases: consumers matched on sentences and one aggregation went silent when a sentence was deleted. Optional, and absent on drivers that predate it — absent means unknown, never 'no reason'. The vocabulary is the failure's STAGE, not the exception class: the three drivers do not share a taxonomy (ios has a typed action error, android throws IllegalArgumentException 75 times, web throws bare Error 80 times), so mapping classes would have produced three different enums. 'setup' and 'teardown' are the case's own fixture steps, which all three drivers record on separate code paths — a teardown failure says nothing about the behaviour under test. 'action' is an action that ran without achieving its effect; 'other' is unclassified and must carry prose in 'error' — a rising 'other' count is the signal that this list is short.

skipReason.description: Why a skipped result was skipped (platform gate vs responsive gate); only meaningful when status is 'skipped'

attempts.description: How many times the case ran in total, retries included (1 = settled on the first run). Absent when the driver does not track attempts. Without this, a pass on the second attempt is byte-identical to a first-run pass and flake rates cannot be computed.

flaky.description: True when the case ultimately passed but needed more than one attempt. Absent when the driver does not track attempts; only meaningful when status is 'passed'
